question: On real, credential-free, publicly reachable websites selected by a preregistered screen that guarantees the substrate actually contains action-gating structure (at least N=3 objects per site whose correct action is not determined by a single unconditional GET from a root observation, with the screen itself calibrated on at least one site known to contain such structure), what fraction of real action-gating objects is reachable by one unconditional GET from a root observation and therefore free to re-derive at the measured observation cost, versus requiring a discovered multi-step path or a state-dependent or non-GET request and therefore costing cross-episode state to know?
hypothesis: On credential-free public websites that genuinely gate actions behind session state, CSRF tokens, or multi-step paths, the re-derivable fraction of action-gating objects is below 0.3, meaning the majority of action-gating structure requires cross-episode knowledge to navigate correctly. This would make C-CROSSSITE transfer testable for the first time in this substrate class.
falsifier: If the measured re-derivable fraction of action-gating objects exceeds 0.8 on the qualifying site set, then C-CROSSSITE inheritance is falsified in the credential-free public HTTP substrate class because almost all action-gating objects are free to re-derive at observation cost, leaving negligible surface for cross-episode inheritance to amortize. The program would then redirect toward self-hosted credentialed substrates where persistence value is not in question.

COLD_REEXPLORATION.description: Fresh exploration each episode. No memory. Re-derives action from root observation each episode. Charged full observation cost (763-token structural representation) per span.
COLD_REEXPLORATION.expected_behavior: Pays full re-derivation cost for every action-gating object. Establishes the upper bound on per-episode cost when no inheritance is used.

NO_MEMORY_DETERMINISTIC.description: No persistent memory. Re-derives action from observation each episode using deterministic policy. Charged full observation cost per span.
NO_MEMORY_DETERMINISTIC.expected_behavior: Similar to COLD_REEXPLORATION but with deterministic re-derivation policy. Serves as a controlled baseline for observation cost.

WITHIN_EPISODE_SCRATCHPAD.description: Within-episode value propagation only. Zero cross-episode retention. Can propagate resource IDs discovered within an episode.
WITHIN_EPISODE_SCRATCHPAD.expected_behavior: Lower cost than cold baselines for multi-step action-gating objects within the same episode, but cannot help across episodes. Establishes the within-episode reuse ceiling.

ORACLE_PERFECT_TRANSFER.description: Oracle that knows the correct stable identifier for every action-gating object from the first episode. Represents perfect cross-episode inheritance with zero re-derivation cost after episode 1.
ORACLE_PERFECT_TRANSFER.expected_behavior: Minimum possible cost after episode 1 (only verification/re-fetch charges). Establishes the lower bound on amortized cost if perfect inheritance were possible.

NULL_COST.description: A cost-based null arm that mimics the CACHE_AND_REVALIDATE structure but uses a randomized/invalid identifier, forcing re-derivation every time while charging the same verification and re-fetch costs. This ensures the null control can fire (produce measurable cost difference) even on substrates where the WRONGNESS null (NULL_STATE_KEYED) cannot because no session-scoped identifiers exist.
NULL_COST.expected_behavior: Cost should equal or exceed COLD_REEXPLORATION (cache overhead + forced re-derivation). If CACHE_AND_REVALIDATE beats this null, the benefit comes from valid identifier binding, not cache structure alone. This null is designed to be discriminating on ANY substrate, including read-only APIs.

site_selection_screen.description: Preregistered screen with explicit criteria to select sites with genuine action-gating structure. Must be calibrated on at least one known qualifying site before TEST site selection.
criteria: Root observation (GET / or equivalent entry point) returns HTML with parseable forms/links

At least 3 action-gating objects per site where correct action requires: (a) POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE with CSRF token or session state, OR (b) multi-step navigation from root (>=2 hops), OR (c) state-dependent response (same URL different content based on prior interaction)
Site reachable with stdlib HTTP only (no JS rendering required for action-gating structure)
site_selection_screen.calibration_site: https://httpbin.org/forms/post (known to have CSRF-like token in form, multi-step POST flow)
site_selection_screen.fallback_if_insufficient: If fewer than 3 qualifying sites found, record exact site URLs and missing criteria (CSRF, session, write verb, multi-step) rather than substituting read-only JSON APIs. This is a valid scientific outcome (surface measurement = 0 in this substrate class).

primary_endpoint.name: action_gating_correctness
primary_endpoint.definition: For each action-gating span, correctness = 1 if the arm's chosen action (method + URL + body) matches the ground-truth required action for that object, verified against response content/structure (not HTTP status alone). Ground truth determined by: (1) successful state transition confirmed by response body parsing, (2) for write verbs, confirmation via subsequent read, (3) for multi-step, completion of full required sequence.
primary_endpoint.dynamic_range_verified: Pre-freeze: baseline arms must show correctness < 1.0 and > 0.0 on qualifying sites, proving the endpoint has dynamic range.

prevalence_estimator.name: rederivable_fraction
prevalence_estimator.definition: Fraction of action-gating spans that are re-derivable: numerator = count of action-gating spans where correct action is determined by single unconditional GET from root observation; denominator = total count of action-gating spans. Both numerator and denominator are counts of spans (same unit).

cost_basis.observation_representation: Body-sensitive: MinimalObservation INCLUDING response body hash and key content fields (not omitted). Tokens computed on full structural representation including body-derived features.
cost_basis.token_to_latency_dollar: UNKNOWN - explicit declaration that no defensible token-to-latency or token-to-dollar mapping exists. Cost reported in tokens and request counts only. Product answer for economics is UNKNOWN.
cost_basis.verification_charge: CACHE_AND_REVALIDATE charges 1 verification_call + 1 re-fetch request per cached action replay.

threshold_satisfiability.pre_freeze_audit: Every frozen threshold must be shown arithmetically reachable at the measured baseline range BEFORE freeze. Specifically: (1) rederivable_fraction threshold 0.3 vs 0.8 must be within [min_baseline, max_baseline] of pilot measurements; (2) action_gating_correctness baseline_max <= 1 - delta for any treatment > baseline + delta clause; (3) cost differences must be measurable given token/request variance observed in pilot.
threshold_satisfiability.baseline_max_rule: For any success criterion of form TREATMENT_metric > BASELINE_metric + delta, must have BASELINE_metric <= 1 - delta at freeze time.

durable_evidence.per_span_records: All SpanRecord fields persisted to JSONL with non-self-referential hashes.
durable_evidence.identifier_classification_log: Every detected identifier with type, subtype, value, source, episode, stability classification.
durable_evidence.response_cache: Response bodies cached for reproducibility (SHA256 + truncated body).

success_criteria_all_required: Site selection screen yields >= 3 qualifying credential-free sites with calibrated action-gating structure (else experiment records surface=0 and redirects per fallback).
Primary endpoint action_gating_correctness shows dynamic range on qualifying sites: COLD_REEXPLORATION correctness in (0.1, 0.9) and ORACLE_PERFECT_TRANSFER correctness > COLD_REEXPLORATION + 0.1.
NULL_COST arm fires: its cost >= COLD_REEXPLORATION cost (proving null is discriminating).
If rederivable_fraction <= 0.3 (with 95% CI upper bound < 0.5): C-CROSSSITE transfer becomes testable for first time in this substrate class -> outcome SUPPORTS continuation of C-CROSSSITE thread.

If rederivable_fraction >= 0.8 (with 95% CI lower bound > 0.6): C-CROSSSITE inheritance falsified in credential-free public HTTP substrate class -> outcome FALSIFIES C-CROSSSITE in this substrate, program redirects to self-hosted credentialed substrates.
If 0.3 < rederivable_fraction < 0.8: INCONCLUSIVE - surface size ambiguous, requires larger sample or different substrate.

cost_secondary.interpretation: If CACHE_AND_REVALIDATE cost < NULL_COST cost with statistical significance, valid identifier binding provides measurable benefit. If not, cache structure alone is insufficient.

abstention_measurement.requirement: All arms must report abstention_rate (decision_path == ABSTAIN). Arms that never abstain on ambiguous action-gating objects are flagged.
abstention_measurement.purpose: Error propagation is a first-class term; abstention measurement is not optional.

product_consequence_positive: If rederivable_fraction <= 0.3: C-CROSSSITE transfer is unblocked for the first time. Four other lanes (Graph, Physics, Product, Intel) receive a measured surface definition for holdout construction. Product can proceed with inheritance economics on a validated target. Runtime knows the substrate requirements for writable controls.
product_consequence_negative: If rederivable_fraction >= 0.8: C-CROSSSITE is falsified in the credential-free public HTTP substrate class. The program redirects toward self-hosted credentialed substrates (where persistence value is not in question) as the next experimental focus. The bounded C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY deterministic-compilation thread remains TERMINATED and must not be re-entered. Frontier continues searching outside the solution basin per its charter.

estimated_cost.compute: stdlib HTTP only, no GPU, no model API

expected_information_gain: This is the upstream precondition nobody has measured. All 48 prior C-CROSSSITE events measured whether a mechanism TRANSFERS; none measured whether there is anything to transfer. A small surface (<=0.3) is a genuine negative for the architecture in the largest accessible domain and redirects the program. A large surface (>=0.8) unblocks C-CROSSSITE for the first time and tells four other lanes what a holdout must contain. Both outcomes are decision-changing. The experiment uses the only substrate class where SPIDER has actually executed on real websites (stdlib HTTP, no browser, no docker, no model key).
